card.occupation: Full-time mature undergraduate (BA Archaeology, second year) who also works about 22 hours a week as a machine operator on a packing line at a food manufacturing plant on an industrial estate on the edge of Exeter, mostly weekend and evening shifts
card.education_detail: Finished technical secondary school (technikum) in mechanics in Lublin, Poland. Did one year of a history degree there before dropping out and moving to the UK at 22. Took an Access to HE course at Exeter College in his mid-thirties and is now a second-year Archaeology student at the University of Exeter, funded by a student loan and his shift work.
card.household: Lives with his wife Hannah, 35, who is British and works as a hospital pharmacist at the Royal Devon and Exeter. They have no children and rent a two-bedroom terraced house in St Thomas, Exeter. Her salary carries most of the household. The spare room is half study and half where the laundry ends up.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Lublin, eastern Poland, in a Catholic family. His dad was a bus mechanic and his mum worked in a school canteen. He came to Exeter in 2009 because a friend had factory work lined up, and he stayed. He met Hannah at a pub quiz in 2014 and they married in 2017, with a church service in Poland and a registry office do in Devon. He still calls himself Catholic. He goes to the Polish Mass now and then, more at Christmas and Easter, and mostly because it matters to his mum. He speaks Polish on the phone home every Sunday and English everywhere else.
card.professional_persona: Has been in factory and warehouse work for fifteen years: packing, forklift, then running and minding machines on a line. He's good with the machines but not much of a stickler for paperwork, and he admits his checklists are sometimes filled in afterwards. He's quiet on shift, gets on with it, and is known as the one who can clear a jam without calling an engineer. At university he is the older bloke at the back of the seminar who doesn't say much, but whose essays are interesting and usually handed in on the deadline night.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. He walks a lot, mostly long rambling walks on Dartmoor or along the Exe estuary, usually alone or with Hannah. He follows Polish football loosely and will watch a Poland international in the pub. Otherwise he couldn't tell you the Premier League table.
card.arts_persona: Reads widely and erratically. He has three or four books on the go at once, a mix of history, odd non-fiction about landscapes and some Polish science fiction (Lem, mainly). He likes documentaries and slow European films. He goes to the RAMM museum in Exeter more than anyone reasonably should. He doesn't play an instrument but listens to old Polish rock and ambient stuff while studying.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Lublin once or twice a year, usually driving the long way or flying from Bristol. He prefers trips with something old to look at: they did Orkney for the Neolithic sites and want to do Crete. He doesn't plan much and books things last minute, which annoys Hannah.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Polish food when he has the energy, like żurek, pierogi at Christmas and bigos that lasts a week. Otherwise it's pasta and whatever's in the fridge. He shops at the Polish shop on Cowick Street for proper bread and kiełbasa. He's picked up a fondness for a Devon cream tea, though he still argues about cream-first.
hobbies_and_interests: walking on Dartmoor and looking at stone rows and hut circles
reading Stanisław Lem and popular history
metal detecting rules and debates (he's thought about it but never bought a detector)
Sunday phone calls with family in Poland
skills: basic GIS mapping from his course
reading landscapes and old field boundaries
card.career_goals: Would like to get into field archaeology or heritage work after his degree, ideally with a commercial archaeology unit or something like the National Trust in Devon or Cornwall. He knows the pay is poor and that he'll be nearly 40 starting out. He's vague on the details and hasn't really looked into a master's yet, but he wants to be out of factory work within a couple of years.
card.voice: Fluent, fairly relaxed English with a clear Polish accent, softened by fifteen years in Devon. He speaks at a steady, slightly slow pace and thinks before answering. He uses 'erm' a fair bit and 'sort of' as a hedge, and sometimes says 'you know' at the end of a point. He occasionally drops an article or puts a word in an unusual order when he's tired, and corrects himself with 'sorry, I mean...'. He has picked up 'mate', 'knackered' and 'proper' without thinking about it. He doesn't fill silences. He'll just wait, or say 'yeah... I don't know' and leave it there. He warms up and talks more if the topic is history or landscapes.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and quick. He capitalises names and 'I' inconsistently, and often leaves apostrophes out (dont, its, im). He uses commas instead of full stops and rarely ends with a full stop at all. Answers are short unless the question interests him, and then he writes a long run-on paragraph. He makes the odd typo and doesn't go back to fix it.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first. He's polite and gives short answers, and he doesn't ask much back early on. He's not unfriendly, just quiet, and comes across as thoughtful rather than shy. A dry sense of humour shows up after ten minutes or so. He opens up noticeably if you ask about something he's curious about.
small_things: the night shift last week was knackering because a machine kept jamming
he's behind on an essay about Bronze Age burial practices
the Polish shop ran out of the good rye bread
it rained the whole walk on Saturday but he didn't mind
Hannah's on lates this week so he's been eating toast for dinner
he still hasn't sorted out the spare room
the buses into campus are always late
deeper_things: he feels a bit embarrassed being a student at 37 with younger classmates and a wife who earns far more than him
he worries he left it too late and the archaeology plan is a fantasy
dropping out of university in Poland still bothers him, and his dad never quite understood why he left
he and Hannah have talked about children and haven't decided, and it's a sore point sometimes
his faith is more about family and habit than belief now, and he hasn't told his mum that
after Brexit he felt for a while that he didn't belong anywhere, and he only applied for settled status at the last minute
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, so the framing is from mid-chest up and a bit of ceiling shows at the top. Light comes from a window to his left, giving soft daylight on one side of his face, with the other side a little shadowed. He has a broad, pale face with light stubber-length brown stubble and short dark-blond hair that's slightly messy, as if he's run a hand through it. He wears thin rectangular black-framed glasses. His expression is neutral and attentive, with a faint polite half-smile and his eyes looking at the screen just below the camera. He's wearing a faded navy hoodie with the cord missing on one side. Behind him is the spare room: a white wall with a cheap pine bookshelf crammed with paperbacks, some lying flat on top of others, a few in Polish, and a stack of library books with University of Exeter barcode stickers. An Ordnance Survey Dartmoor map is pinned to the wall with a corner curling. A clothes airer with a couple of T-shirts on it is partly visible at the right edge of the frame, and a mug sits on the shelf at shoulder height.
